stanzas: Ich weiß nicht, was soll es bedeuten,
Das kommt mir nicht aus dem Sinn.
Die Luft ist kühl und es dunkelt,
Sie kämmt es mit gold’nem Kamme,
Er schaut nur hinauf in die Höh’.
Und das hat mit ihrem Singen
orig.credit: Heinrich Heine, Buch der Lieder (1827; written 1824)
orig.page: Ich weiß nicht, was soll es bedeuten

stanzas: I do not know what it should mean
The air is cool and it grows dark,
The summit of the mountain sparkles
She combs it with a golden comb,
And sings a song as she does;
The boatman in his little boat
Is seized by it with wild woe;
He does not see the rocky reefs,
He looks only up into the height.
In the end boatman and boat;

notes: line 1.3: 'Mährchen' is the old spelling of 'Märchen': a tale, legend or fairy tale.
line 3.2: 'wunderbar' can describe how she sits (wondrously, marvellously) or the maiden herself (wonderful); the word order allows both.
line 4.4: 'Melodei' is an old, poetic form of 'Melodie', chosen for the rhyme with 'dabei'.
line 5.1-2: literally 'The boatman in the small boat / it seizes with wild woe': 'es' is the song (or her singing), the subject; the boatman is the object. 'Weh' is pain, woe or longing.
line 6.1: 'verschlingen' is present tense, as in the German ('I believe the waves swallow'), with the sense 'swallowed up' or 'will swallow up'.
line 6.2: 'Kahn' is a small boat or skiff, a second word for the 'kleines Schiff' of 5.1.
line 6.4: 'Lore-Ley' is the name of the rock above the Rhine and of the maiden Heine places on it; kept as a name. 'gethan' is the old spelling of 'getan' (done).
